transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-10
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood SE), Dr. Alan Cho (CTO - Emerald), Marta Ruiz (Privacy Officer), Leo Zhang (ML Eng), Simone Park (Product)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Quick scoping for a 4-week POC focused on data handling and benchmarks. Key topics: PII redaction, logging and retention policy, prompt storage concerns, workload sizing and benchmark plan, timeline for pilot and success criteria. Action items and next steps captured at end.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, i'll hand it to priya to kick off the agenda but main thing today is to align on data handling requirements for the POC and what success looks like
[00:18] Priya: yeah thanks jordan, hi all, quick run-down - we're proposing a 4-week POC, two phases: ingestion & safety (week 1-2) and benchmarks + tuning (week 3-4). we want to confirm what kinds of PII are in-scope, whether you need full private deployment or just VPC peering, and the benchmark metrics - latency, tp50/tp95, and quality regressions you care about
[00:35] Dr. Cho: sounds good. to be clear, our main blockers are regulatory: patient identifiers, PHI redaction, and auditability for retention. Marta can talk specifics
[00:50] Marta: right - we have PHI like patient name, mrn, ssn-ish numbers, appointment notes that mention health conditions. for the POC we want two options: 1) no raw prompt retention, and 2) if any logs are kept they must be redacted and retained for no longer than 30 days unless under legal hold. also need audit logs exported to our SIEM
[01:12] Priya: ok got it. Redwood supports per-customer retention settings on Dedicated and Private. hosted paths store request logs by default but you can opt-out; we also have automated redaction pipelines that run as a pre-write hook, we'll share the current regex & NER-based approach - but note, NER sometimes misses custom MRN formats
[01:35] Leo: NER misses are our worry - we have a bunch of internal codes, also free-text clinical notes with shorthand. is there support for custom redaction rules?
[01:48] Samir: absolutely, you can supply custom redaction patterns and a training list; we can also do a deterministic tokenizer for MRNs and apply hashing or tokenization before sending to the model. For maximum privacy, we suggest client-side redaction or tokenization in your app before hitting our API
[02:10] Simone: client-side sounds heavy for product, curious about tradeoffs - latency and feature parity?
[02:22] Priya: yeah tradeoffs - client-side redaction reduces exposure but increases integration effort and shifts failure modes to you. server-side redaction is easier but you have to trust pre-processing. with Dedicated/Private we can enable an end-to-end encrypted path and KMS so logs at rest are encrypted with your key
[02:40] Dr. Cho: what about prompt storage? we embed patient snippets in prompts for summarization - do we need to store prompts to reproduce outputs for audits?
[02:55] Jordan: good question. there's a couple patterns: 1) ephemeral mode where prompts are not stored (we don't persist request body), 2) store prompts but redact PHI first, or 3) store prompts encrypted with customer-managed key and only keep them for X days. For an audit you could keep a hash of the prompt + metadata so you can prove request happened without exposing content
[03:18] Marta: the hash idea might satisfy legal - but for medical review we often need full context; we'd prefer encrypt+retain for 90 days but legal wants 30 by default, unless a legal hold extends it
[03:31] Priya: ok we should capture that as configuration - default 30-day retention, option to extend to 90 for specific cases under legal hold, and support for customer-managed KMS so Redwood cannot decrypt logs without access
[03:45] Leo: on logging: do you log intermediate tokens? we use streaming in product - we don't want raw token logs stored anywhere
[03:55] Samir: streaming doesn't imply persistent token logs. we can stream to the client and not keep intermediate tokens; our diagnostic logs can be configured to either store full token-level traces or only aggregates. for POC we'll set diagnostics to minimal and only capture metrics you approve
[04:15] [crosstalk] Marta: and SSO for accessing logs?
[04:22] Priya: yes we support SAML SSO and RBAC on the console; admin roles can be restricted to specific teams. also audit logs include who viewed what and when
[04:35] Jordan: switching gears to sizing and benchmarks - Leo can you share current throughput expectations?
[04:44] Leo: currently we expect spike loads up to 40 qps for the summarization endpoint during business hours, average 8 qps; typical prompt length ~600 tokens, response ~200 tokens. 95th latency target we'd like under 700ms for user-facing flows
[05:03] Priya: cool, that's helpful. for the POC we'll simulate 50 qps at various concurrency and measure tp50/tp95/tp99 and token cost. we'll also run quality evals vs your golden set - how many labeled cases do you have?
[05:20] Simone: we have ~1,200 annotated summaries, can share a 200-case evaluation set for the POC and a larger offline set for model tuning
[05:30] Jordan: success criteria - let's align: 1) functional: accurate PHI redaction in >98% of sampled cases, 2) perf: tp95 < 800ms at 40 qps load, 3) cost: token cost below your target (we'll include estimated savings from batching/caching), 4) integration: ability to configure retention and KMS. agree?
[05:51] Marta: those look reasonable, but add: privacy: no plaintext prompts retained unless encrypted and authorized; and audit: ability to export audit logs within 24 hours
[06:05] Priya: noted - we'll update success criteria doc. also competitors - Dr. Cho asked earlier about other vendors; we discussed Anthropic and OpenAI briefly. Redwood differentiator is Dedicated/Private with configurable retention and KMS plus per-route observability
[06:24] Dr. Cho: timeline - we need POC results before April 30th, ideally. Can you do a 4-week POC starting 3/22?
[06:34] Jordan: 3/22 start is doable. Week 0 (this week): define scope and access. Week 1-2: integration and data handling validation (redaction, retention). Week 3-4: benchmark runs and evals. Final report and go/no-go by 4/23-4/30.
[06:52] Leo: what environment? hosted with VPC peering or Private?
[06:58] Priya: recommendation: start with Dedicated (reserved pool) with VPC peering so you get isolation and we can enable customer KMS. If regulatory pushes, move to Private on-prem later. Dedicated gives us enough control for redaction and retention testing without full on-prem integration during POC
[07:14] Marta: Dedicated + KMS sounds fine for now. but we need proof that Redwood or support can't access decrypted logs - is that in the SOC2 docs?
[07:24] Samir: yes, SOC2 covers access controls; with customer-managed KMS we do not hold keys. we'll include the KMS flow diagram and explain key policies in the doc we share.
[07:35] Jordan: benchmarks - Priya will own the workload plan; Samir will set up a synthetic harness and run baseline on the model variants. items to measure: token throughput, latency percentiles, cold-start scenarios, and quality regression against your eval set
[08:00] Leo: for model variants can you test quantized vs fp16? we care about cost but not at expense of hallucinations
[08:12] Priya: yes we'll include model variants and simple quantization profiles; we'll run a small human eval on hallucination rate for the eval set
[08:22] Simone: what about prompt storage for auditing - if we encrypt prompts and store, how do we allow Emerald to decrypt for legal review?
[08:32] Samir: two options: 1) provide an admin UI to request decryption that requires dual control (customer approves), or 2) provide an export (encrypted) to your side for decryption with your key. we'll include both options in the doc
[08:46] Marta: prefer option 2 - keep the decryption control on our side
[08:50] Priya: noted. we'll configure export-only retention for encrypted prompts so data never gets decrypted on Redwood side by default
[09:02] Jordan: risk points called out: custom MRN formats may require rule tuning, NER won't catch everything, and streaming diagnostics must be disabled for POC unless explicitly requested. we'll capture mitigations
[09:18] Dr. Cho: any SLA during POC? we need at least 99% availability for test window and a run-book for incidents
[09:26] Jordan: we'll commit to operational window and provide an incident runbook for the POC. Dedicated includes monitoring; we'll provide on-call contacts for the test window
[09:38] Marta: compliance questions: can you provide encryption-at-rest details, key rotation policy, and whether audit logs include request bodies or only metadata?
[09:48] Priya: encryption at rest uses AES-256; with customer-managed KMS we support rotation and no key access for Redwood. audit logs by default include metadata (who, when, model). request bodies only if you enable prompt retention - we'll default that off for POC
[10:02] Leo: about traffic shaping - we may want to replay a week of traffic anonymized. is there a replay tool?
[10:10] Samir: yes we can ingest anonymized payloads; better if you strip PHI client-side first. we also provide a replay harness to simulate production concurrency patterns
[10:20] Simone: documentation - can you share a short checklist we can run internally so we can provision the required IAM roles and network access?
[10:29] Jordan: yes - Priya will send a checklist (VPC CIDR, allowed ports, service account, SAML metadata)
[10:35] Marta: on legal hold - how fast can retention be extended if legal requires?
[10:40] Priya: we support immediate flagging of a set of records to indefinite hold; for POC we can demonstrate the workflow. we'll capture sample API calls for setting legal hold
[10:50] Jordan: ok, i want to recap success criteria and next steps: success criteria we agreed earlier (redaction >98%, tp95 <800ms at 40 qps, encrypted retention option, audit export), next steps are Jordan to send scope and pricing, Priya to send architecture & SOC2 summary, Leo to share payloads, Samir to draft benchmark plan, and schedule kickoff for 3/22. any objections?
[12:17] Dr. Cho: none from me, looks good
[12:24] Marta: fine, please include the 30-day default retention in the POC doc and the encrypted export option
[12:30] Leo: i'll get the sample payloads by monday
[12:35] Jordan: perfect, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the kickoff and share the docs. thanks everyone
[12:42] Priya: thanks all
[12:45] [END]
